item.title: Middle East war live: Rubio says announcement on Iran war possible later Sunday
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Sunday said an announcement on the Iran war could be possible later in the day. While US media has reported that a deal would include a commitment from Tehran to hand over its stockpile of highly enriched uranium, an Iranian source told Reuters this was not the case. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: Israel's Ben-Gvir sees 'no innocent people in Gaza or even Europe': Journalist Gideon Levy
item.description: FRANCE 24's François Picard welcomes veteran Israeli journalist and Haaretz columnist Gideon Levy. He offers a scathing analysis of Israeli politics, the Gaza war, the unprecedented rise of xenophobic nationalism and Israel's growing dependence on the United States. Speaking from Tel Aviv amid mounting electoral tensions, Levy argues that "everything – war and peace, domestic politics, legislation – is now covered by the shadow of the upcoming elections".

item.title: 'Cold, pragmatic relationship': UAE-Israel ties driven by defence and technology
item.description: Nadia Massih is pleased to welcome Dr Andreas Krieg, Senior Lecturer at the School of Security Studies at King's College London and Fellow at the Institute of Middle Eastern Studies. According to Krieg, "Iran is fighting a war against the global economy." By targeting the UAE, and especially Dubai, Tehran is not merely retaliating militarily but seeking to exploit what Krieg calls the "Achilles heel" of the international system: the Gulf's hyperconnected financial and logistical infrastructure.

item.title: Ben Gvir's flotilla video: Netanyahu has 'lost control of the government'
item.description: Italy and Spain are calling on the EU to sanction Israel's far-right national security minister, over his posting of a video showing detained Gaza-bound activists forced to their knees with their hands bound. The footage – which showed Itamar Ben-Gvir heckling activists while waving an Israeli flag – has prompted a global outcry. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks to Yossi Mekelberg, senior consulting fellow at Chatham House.

item.title: 'Significant movement here in Washington': US and Iran report progress towards deal on ending war
item.description: FRANCE 24 correspondent Fraser Jackson speaks from Washington, DC on the reported progress in the talks on ending the US-Israeli war on Iran.

item.title: Iran, US and Pakistan report progress in talks on ending war
item.description: Washington, Tehran and mediator Islamabad all said on Saturday that progress had been made on ending the US-Israeli war on Iran, with a Pakistani security official saying that a memorandum of understanding was being "fine-tuned".

item.title: War in the Middle East: US-Iran talks make headway
item.description: Anahita Motazed Rad, Associate Fellow at the London School of Economics, is our guest.

item.title: US and Iran are ‘getting a lot closer’ to finalising agreement, Trump says
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Saturday told US broadcaster CBS that Tehran and Washington were "getting a lot closer" to finalising an agreement between the two countries. Iran earlier said that it was in the “final stage” of drafting an agreement with the US to end the US-Israeli war on Iran, the Islamic Republic’s state media reported. Read our liveblog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: Freed Gaza flotilla activists allege Israeli abuse including rape
item.description: Activists released from Israeli custody after being detained on a flotilla trying to bring aid to Gaza were subjected to abuse, organisers said on Friday, with several hospitalised with injuries and at least 15 reporting sexual assaults, including rape.

item.title: France condemns Israel as it deports 37 French nationals over Gaza flotilla
item.description: All 37 French nationals detained aboard a Gaza-bound aid flotilla to Turkey were deported by Israel on Thursday. Paris summoned a senior Israeli diplomat over a video showing the country's national security minister taunting the multinational group of activists while they were being detained.
